entry.title: Fresh lemon juice soap recipe - a natural citric acid and colour boost! (full tutorial)

media:group.media:title: Fresh lemon juice soap recipe - a natural citric acid and colour boost! (full tutorial)
media:group.media:description:
In this video, I’m making cold process soap with fresh lemon juice. Using lemon juice is both fun and practical: it’s a natural source of citric acid, which helps reduce soap scum, extend shelf life of handmade soap recipes, and boost lather thanks to the natural sugars.
I’ll walk you step by step through the process—squeezing and freezing the juice, preparing the oils and and lye solution and pouring into flower molds. I’ll also share why this batch took a little longer to saponify and how I tested to make sure it was successful.
*If you're brand new to soap making* Please take the time to educate yourself thoroughly on the safety aspects of handmade soap making. These videos are important: Safety Essentials https://youtu.be/EZTsW9UvNmU Soap Making Tutorial and Recipe for Absolute Beginners https://youtu.be/lBc-dWQmFIM pH testing with strips https://youtu.be/EZTsW9UvNmU The old fashioned (but good) Zap Test https://youtu.be/SS14Gsl4gKQ
*Timestamps* 00:00 Introduction and why lemon juice 01:01 Benefits of citric acid in soap 01:39 Washing and prepping the lemons 02:05 Measuring the juice 04:24 Choosing and preparing oils 05:55 Safety first: handling sodium hydroxide 06:32 Selecting essential oils 07:43 Mixing everything up 09:42 Pouring into molds 10:48 Spraying with alcohol and insulating the soap 11:10 Saponification delays and troubleshooting 12:41 Results after three days 13:25 Final thoughts and lather test

In today's video, I'm sharing a simple and cost-effective laundry soap recipe using store-bought soap—perfect for beginners or anyone looking to save on soap-making ingredients. I'll walk you through each step, from choosing the right soap to mixing it with borax and washing soda, ending up with an affordable and effective 10-liter batch of liquid laundry soap.
